caption: Figure 1: Illustration of diversity preservation in SFT. While pre-trained LLMs produce diverse outputs, these often lack proper formatting. Standard SFT using CE improves readability but reduces diversity. We aim to maintain output diversity while enhancing the readability of LLMs' responses.
Figure 2: Comparison of learning schemes: CE v.s. GEM (β = 0). The arrows illustrate the probability movement directions during the learning process, with Token 3 as the target token.
Figure3: Illustration of the meta-controller q.
Figure5: Performance of test-time scaling. The results demonstrate that GEM achieves better performance with the same sampling budget and is more efficient in reaching comparable performance.
Figure 4: Enhancing output diversity boosts the win rate when using BoN.
Figure 6: Performance on tasks from the OpenLLM leaderboard. The results indicate that GEM outperforms CE, demonstrating a lower alignment tax.
Figure 7: Staying close to the pretrained model helps mitigate forgetting.
